Status: Wave 293 accepted (6.3): three Falcon domain and session frames

Method.evidence: Three frames read from their formatters and accessor types. Class838 prints SNo={0} DoA={1} from b(), a(): the first getter pairs with a setter taking Knx.Falcon.SerialNumber and the second (offset 6) with a Knx.Falcon.DomainAddress setter guarded by its own DoA must be {0} octets but is {1} check. Class900 prints SNo={0} IA={1} with the same serial number pair and an IndividualAddress pair at offset 6. Class851 prints Session Timeout={0} from a(), a 16-bit value at offset 4, and the sibling getter at the same base drives the setter that takes a SessionType. Each type also has a byte[] factory that only wraps the caller buffer. Class834 (Type=0 DoA={0} Start={1} Range={2}) needs its getters types before Start and Range can be told apart, so it stays unresolved.
Method.themes: Accessor types are the pairing key when the offsets are identical (the DoA/IA/SNo setters are told apart by their parameter types). Remaining worklist: Class834 (getter types), Class824/Class825 (byte setters through the base helper), Class938 (formatter prints only a constant), Class871 (four packed 16-bit fields), and the five-row types Class904/Class905/Class829/Class835/Class840.
